passages.text: Then Zophar the Naamathite replied: “Should this stream of words go unanswered and such a speaker be vindicated?
passages.sermon:
Zophar was a Naamathite.
Zophar replied to Job.
Zophar heard Job speak many words.
Zophar asked a question.
He said, “Should this stream of words go unanswered?
Should a man who talks so much be considered right?”
passages.original: וַ֭יַּעַן צֹפַ֥ר הַֽנַּעֲמָתִ֗י וַיֹּאמַֽר׃ הֲרֹ֣ב דְּ֭בָרִים לֹ֣א יֵעָנֶ֑ה וְאִם־ אִ֖ישׁ שְׂפָתַ֣יִם יִצְדָּֽק׃

passages.text: Should your babbling put others to silence? Will you scoff without rebuke?
passages.sermon:
Zophar the Naamathite speaks to Job.
Zophar hears Job's many words.
Zophar asks Job a question.
He says, "Should your empty talk make others silent?"
He asks, "Can you mock without anyone correcting you?"
passages.original: בַּ֭דֶּיךָ מְתִ֣ים יַחֲרִ֑ישׁו וַ֝תִּלְעַ֗ג וְאֵ֣ין מַכְלִֽם׃

passages.text: You have said, ‘My doctrine is sound, and I am pure in Your sight.’
passages.sermon:
Zophar the Naamathite spoke to Job.
Zophar said, “You have claimed something.”
You said, ‘My teaching is pure.’
You said, ‘I am clean in God’s eyes.’
passages.original: וַ֭תֹּאמֶר זַ֣ךְ לִקְחִ֑י וּ֝בַ֗ר הָיִ֥יתִי בְעֵינֶֽיךָ׃

passages.text: But if only God would speak and open His lips against you, and disclose to you the secrets of wisdom, for true wisdom has two sides. Know then that God exacts from you less than your iniquity deserves.
passages.sermon:
God is all-wise and all-knowing.
God holds the secrets of wisdom.
God’s wisdom has many sides.
If only God would speak to you.
If only God would open His lips to you.
God could reveal the secrets of wisdom to you.
You would see that wisdom is deep and complex.
Know this: God punishes you less than your sins deserve.
passages.original: וְֽאוּלָ֗ם מִֽי־ יִתֵּ֣ן אֱל֣וֹהַּ דַּבֵּ֑ר וְיִפְתַּ֖ח שְׂפָתָ֣יו עִמָּֽךְ׃ וְיַגֶּד־ לְךָ֨׀ תַּֽעֲלֻמ֣וֹת חָכְמָה֮ כִּֽי־ כִפְלַ֪יִם לְֽת֫וּשִׁיָּ֥ה וְדַ֡ע כִּֽי־ יַשֶּׁ֥ה לְךָ֥ אֱ֝ל֗וֹהַ מֵעֲוֺנֶֽךָ׃

passages.text: Can you fathom the deep things of God or discover the limits of the Almighty?
passages.sermon:
God is the Almighty.
God has deep things.
You cannot fully understand the deep things of God.
You cannot discover the limits of the Almighty.
passages.original: הַחֵ֣קֶר אֱל֣וֹהַ תִּמְצָ֑א אִ֤ם עַד־ תַּכְלִ֖ית שַׁדַּ֣י תִּמְצָֽא׃

passages.text: They are higher than the heavens—what can you do? They are deeper than Sheol—what can you know?
passages.sermon:
God’s ways are higher than the heavens.
You cannot do anything to reach them.
God’s wisdom is deeper than Sheol, the place of the dead.
You cannot know or understand it fully.
passages.original: גָּבְהֵ֣י שָׁ֭מַיִם מַה־ תִּפְעָ֑ל עֲמֻקָּ֥ה מִ֝שְּׁא֗וֹל מַה־ תֵּדָֽע׃

passages.text: Their measure is longer than the earth and wider than the sea.
passages.sermon:
God’s ways are vast.
God’s understanding is greater than the earth’s length.
God’s wisdom is wider than the sea.
No one can measure God’s greatness.
passages.original: אֲרֻכָּ֣ה מֵאֶ֣רֶץ מִדָּ֑הּ וּ֝רְחָבָ֗ה מִנִּי־ יָֽם׃

passages.text: If He comes along to imprison you, or convenes a court, who can stop Him?
passages.sermon:
God is all-powerful.
God can come and take a person away.
God can imprison anyone.
God can gather people for judgment.
No one can stop God.
No one can oppose His actions.
passages.original: אִם־ יַחֲלֹ֥ף וְיַסְגִּ֑יר וְ֝יַקְהִ֗יל וּמִ֣י יְשִׁיבֶֽנּוּ׃

passages.text: Surely He knows the deceit of men. If He sees iniquity, does He not take note?
passages.sermon:
God knows every person.
God knows when people deceive.
God sees every sin.
God does not ignore evil.
God notices wrongdoing.
passages.original: כִּי־ ה֭וּא יָדַ֣ע מְתֵי־ שָׁ֑וְא וַיַּרְא־ אָ֝֗וֶן וְלֹ֣א יִתְבּוֹנָֽן׃

passages.text: But a witless man can no more become wise than the colt of a wild donkey can be born a man!
passages.sermon:
A foolish man cannot become wise.
A man without understanding will not gain wisdom.
A wild donkey’s colt cannot be born as a man.
In the same way, a witless man cannot become wise.
passages.original: וְאִ֣ישׁ נָ֭בוּב יִלָּבֵ֑ב וְעַ֥יִר פֶּ֝֗רֶא אָדָ֥ם יִוָּלֵֽד׃

passages.text: As for you, if you direct your heart and lift up your hands to Him, if you put away the iniquity in your hand, and allow no injustice to dwell in your tents, then indeed you will lift up your face without shame; you will stand firm and unafraid.
passages.sermon:
God sees all people.
God knows if someone is deceitful.
God notices every sin.
You are a person who seeks God.
If you prepare your heart for God, He will see it.
If you lift your hands to God in prayer, He will hear you.
If you remove sin from your actions, God will know.
If you do not allow injustice in your home, God will see your honesty.
Then you will be able to lift your face without shame.
You will stand strong.
You will not be afraid.
passages.original: אִם־ אַ֭תָּ֗ה הֲכִינ֣וֹתָ לִבֶּ֑ךָ וּפָרַשְׂתָּ֖ אֵלָ֣יו כַּפֶּֽךָ׃ אִם־ אָ֣וֶן בְּ֭יָדְךָ הַרְחִיקֵ֑הוּ וְאַל־ תַּשְׁכֵּ֖ן בְּאֹהָלֶ֣יךָ עַוְלָֽה׃ כִּי־ אָ֤ז׀ תִּשָּׂ֣א פָנֶ֣יךָ מִמּ֑וּם וְהָיִ֥יתָ מֻ֝צָ֗ק וְלֹ֣א תִירָֽא׃

passages.text: For you will forget your misery, recalling it only as waters gone by.
passages.sermon:
You are a person who turns to God and puts away sin.
You will forget your misery.
You will remember your suffering like water that has passed by.
Your pain will not trouble you anymore.
Your troubles will seem distant and gone.
passages.original: כִּי־ אַ֭תָּה עָמָ֣ל תִּשְׁכָּ֑ח כְּמַ֖יִם עָבְר֣וּ תִזְכֹּֽר׃

passages.text: Your life will be brighter than noonday; its darkness will be like the morning.
passages.sermon:
God promises hope to those who turn to Him.
He gives new life to those who repent and seek Him.
Your life will shine brighter than the noonday sun.
Even your darkness will become like the morning light.
passages.original: וּֽ֭מִצָּהֳרַיִם יָק֣וּם חָ֑לֶד תָּ֝עֻ֗פָה כַּבֹּ֥קֶר תִּהְיֶֽה׃

passages.text: You will be secure, because there is hope, and you will look around and lie down in safety.
passages.sermon:
You will feel secure.
You will have hope.
You will look around with confidence.
You will lie down in safety.
passages.original: וּֽ֭בָטַחְתָּ כִּי־ יֵ֣שׁ תִּקְוָ֑ה וְ֝חָפַרְתָּ֗ לָבֶ֥טַח תִּשְׁכָּֽב׃

passages.text: You will lie down without fear, and many will court your favor.
passages.sermon: You will lie down.\r\nYou will not be afraid.\r\nMany people will seek your favor.
passages.original: וְֽ֭רָבַצְתָּ וְאֵ֣ין מַחֲרִ֑יד וְחִלּ֖וּ פָנֶ֣יךָ רַבִּֽים׃

passages.text: But the eyes of the wicked will fail, and escape will elude them; they will hope for their last breath.”
passages.sermon:
The wicked are people who do evil.
Their eyes will fail.
They will not find escape.
They will lose all hope.
They will hope only for their last breath.
passages.original: וְעֵינֵ֥י רְשָׁעִ֗ים תִּ֫כְלֶ֥ינָה וּ֭מָנוֹס אָבַ֣ד מִנְהֶ֑ם וְ֝תִקְוָתָ֗ם מַֽפַּח־ נָֽפֶשׁ׃פ
